mia: Starting a canary for Lacerta14b (int4) — noticing intermittent OOMs on long-context docs. Canary settings: batch=10, max_new_tokens=300, prefetch=enabled, quant=q4_k_m_pack. Kicking off a 2k prompt perf run.

alex: Thanks. Can you paste a short repro + the exact OOM trace? Also which node pool?

mia: Node pool: canary-gpu-2. Repro (short): send a 6-turn dialogue with a 6k-token context + request 250 tokens. OOM excerpt: 
```
[OOM] cudaMalloc failed at serving::kv::alloc
node: canary-gpu-2-11
heap: attempted alloc 40MB, free 12MB
stack: runtime::kv_cache::reserve -> kv_slot::grow -> cudaMalloc -> OOM
```

ryan: Sounds like kv-slot growth during long generations. Two things to try quickly: 1) soft cap on KV: `max_kv_bytes=50MB`; 2) reduce concurrent prefetched reads: `max_prefetch_ops=3`. Also try lowering default max_new_tokens to 150 for the canary traffic.

mia: I toggled max_kv_bytes=50MB and set max_prefetch_ops=3 in the canary config. Early run: no OOMs so far across 100 long requests. Metrics: P50=140ms, P95=590ms, throughput -25% vs baseline. GPU mem peak: 33.1 GiB.

alex: Throughput hit isn't great. We should consider per-request routing: estimate response length at request time and send >200-token requests to Lacerta13b-int8. Implement this as a router policy: if est_out_tokens > 200 -> route. Also add metric tag on those routed requests so we can compare quality.

ryan: Agree. Also test a middle-ground variant: batch=6, prefetch=false, kv_cushion=0.10. That sometimes reduces p95 with small perf loss. And enable `kv_slot_compact=true` to reclaim fragmented KV slots.

mia: I'll run three experiments A/B/C: A) conservative cap (max_kv_bytes=50MB) + prefetch=off + batch=6; B) soft-evict (evict_threshold=0.8) + prefetch=on + batch=8; C) routing only + default canary config. For each, I'll run eval set: short-QA (1k), summarization (300), long-doc QA (200). Will capture QA-F1, rouge and an hallucination check.

alex: For the hallucination check, run the simple reference overlap + a synthetic negative prompt to detect made-up facts. Label any sample with >0.25 hallucination score as fail.

mia: Noted. Quick ask: does anyone object to adding a temporary console alert if OOM rate > 0.05% during the canary? That helps early stop.

ryan: Good idea. Set alert threshold 0.05% for canary-ml. If triggered, auto-scale down Lacerta14b traffic to 0 and leave Lacerta13b handling all.

mia: Deploy-bot: starting variant runs now. I'll post the 30m report here.

deploy-bot: Canary job r-20260324-09 launched on pool canary-gpu-2 (15% capacity). Monitoring hooks active.

alex: Also check kernel selection: switch to narrow-kernel-path for long contexts so memory locality is better. Try `kernel_pref=local_first`.

mia: Will flip kernel_pref for experiment B. Experiment A running now. Back soon with numbers. Thanks! :rocket:
